result:
If I could change the world in one way, I'd give people a reliable, widespread capacity for genuine empathy — the ability to vividly understand others' experiences and needs, not just to feel sympathy at a distance.

That single change would alter politics, reduce violence, improve cooperation on shared problems (poverty, health, climate), and shift priorities from short-term self-interest to long-term collective flourishing. With deeper empathy, policies would be judged by real human impact, businesses would design for dignity, and everyday interactions would be kinder and more constructive. It wouldn't erase trade-offs or complexity, but it would make finding humane, durable solutions far more likely.
